finding.claim: Unauthenticated SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is f-string interpolated into a LIKE clause, allowing UNION-based read of any table in shop.db (schema enumeration via sqlite_master). Writes are blocked by sqlite3 single-statement execution. Severity CRITICAL, conditional on shop.db holding sensitive data and no upstream WAF.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter q, read at app.py:11 via request.args.get, no authentication required
finding.sink: db.execute() at app.py:12 with f-string SQL construction

trace.note: /search route registered with no authentication decorator
term = request.args.get('q', '') takes attacker-controlled input with no validation
f-string interpolates term into SQL text inside LIKE '%...%' with no escaping or binding
db.execute runs on shared module-level connection defined at app.py:6
jsonify(rows) returns injected result set to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No authentication on route (app.py:9-10); no input validation or length limit; no parameter binding on this path (contrast /product at app.py:18 and /by-owner at app.py:25, which bind); sqlite3 execute single-statement restriction blocks stacked writes but not UNION reads; no WAF or proxy rules in repository (unverified); bind address and debug flag live in startup code not present in repo (unverified).

verdict.guard_found: none. The /search route (app.py:9-10) has no auth decorator. q is taken raw at app.py:11 with no validation or length limit. app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL via f-string with no binding. The shared connection at app.py:6 is used directly. The only control is Python sqlite3's single-statement restriction, which blocks stacked writes but not a UNION read. The parameterized routes at app.py:18 and app.py:25 do not cover this path.
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.py:9-13 exactly: an anonymous request reaches the f-string SQL at app.py:12 with the raw q value from app.py:11, and nothing in the repo escapes or binds it, so a quote-breakout UNION SELECT against sqlite_master (for example) returns attacker-chosen rows through jsonify at app.py:13. Deployment controls (WAF, bind address, debug flag) are outside the repo and unverified, but they would not block the code-level flaw, and the CRITICAL severity rating is a judgment I did not verify.
